rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a material template. It shares the specific entrepreneurship-centered commemorative structure, describes entrepreneurs as risk-takers who promote economic growth, and culminates in nearly matching operative language proclaiming an observance and calling on all Americans to commemorate it with appropriate activities. C09 and C02 have similar proclamation mechanics, but their overlap is primarily conventional observance language without the distinctive entrepreneurship connection.

shared_material.child_excerpt: entrepreneurs from every walk of life make invaluable contributions to the American experience—turning bold ideas into real progress
shared_material.parent_excerpt: We are all inspired by the example our entrepreneurs have set.
shared_material.explanation: Both proclamations celebrate entrepreneurs as exemplary contributors to national progress.

shared_material.child_excerpt: those who take a risk and put in the hard work required to get a new venture off the ground
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Those who undertake the journey must be talented, determined, and brave. But America has a history of rewarding risk-takers
shared_material.explanation: Both frame entrepreneurship through risk-taking, determination, and the difficulty of launching businesses.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby proclaim November 2016 as National Entrepreneurship Month. I call upon all Americans to commemorate this month with appropriate programs and activities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby proclaim September 24 through September 30, 1995, as "Minority Enterprise Development Week." I call on all Americans to commemorate this event with appropriate ceremonies and activities
shared_material.explanation: This is a close parallel in the operative sequence and wording: proclaim an entrepreneurship-related observance, then call on all Americans to commemorate it through appropriate activities.
